chapter.title: Why Boundaries Exist
chapter.description: What happens without one, and the two lifecycle methods that make one.

blocks.text: Since React 16, an error thrown during rendering unmounts the **entire** component tree. The reasoning is that a half-rendered interface is worse than none: a banking app showing the wrong balance is more dangerous than one showing an error.
An **error boundary** catches errors below it and renders a fallback instead, so the failure is contained to one part of the screen.
There is still no hook equivalent. A boundary implements one or both of two lifecycle methods.

items: `getDerivedStateFromError` runs during rendering, so it must be pure - just return the state that shows the fallback.
`componentDidCatch` runs after the commit, so logging, analytics and anything with a side effect goes there. It also receives the component stack.

blocks.text: In practice most teams use `react-error-boundary`, which wraps this in a hook-friendly API with reset support. Understanding the class version first makes that library obvious rather than magic.

blocks.text: A boundary catches errors thrown during rendering, in lifecycle methods, and in constructors of the components **below** it. Everything else escapes.
Handlers run outside the render cycle, so React cannot intercept them. Use a normal `try`/`catch`.
A rejected promise or an error inside `setTimeout` happens long after rendering finished. To route it to a boundary, catch it and set state that throws during the next render.
Boundaries do not catch errors during server-side rendering. Frameworks provide their own error handling for that phase - `error.js` in Next.js, for example.
Not caught: errors in the boundary itself
A boundary cannot catch its own errors. If the fallback throws, the error propagates to the next boundary up - so keep fallbacks extremely simple.
A fallback that renders the failing component again, or that formats untrusted error data, can throw and take down the boundary you were relying on. Plain text and a retry button is the safe design.
